context:
Patient: 59F, breast cancer survivor (2016: dose-dense AC, cumulative doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left breast RT, on anastrozole), presents with left axillary mass, fevers to 38.4 C, drenching night sweats; ECOG 1, LDH 510. Non-GCB DLBCL (MYC 45%, BCL2 70%, FISH negative for rearrangements), PET nodes above and below the diaphragm plus splenic nodules, marrow negative, and new LVEF 45% (62% in 2016) with GLS -14%.
What this case tests: Spleen is a nodal site under Lugano, so stage is III, not IV, and IPI is 2. | Double-expressor by IHC but FISH-negative, so not double-hit; no intensification to DA-EPOCH-R. | Prior doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left chest RT and LVEF 62% to 45% mean standard full-dose R-CHOP / Pola-R-CHP is not safe as is. | Treatment must stay curative: anthracycline-free (R-CEOP / R-GCVP) or cardio-protected regimen, with cardio-oncology input and cardioprotective drugs. | CNS-IPI 2 with no high-risk sites: no routine CNS prophylaxis.

answer.diagnosis:
Newly diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, NOS (ICD-10-CM C83.30; SNOMED 109969005), presenting in the left axillary node in a 59-year-old woman with ER+/HER2- left breast carcinoma in remission since 2016.

This is a NEW PRIMARY LYMPHOMA, NOT RECURRENT OR METASTATIC BREAST CANCER. The referral question (recurrence vs other) is answered definitively: the excisional biopsy (2026-08-25) shows a large-cell B-lineage neoplasm (CD20 diffuse strong, PAX5+, CD19+, kappa light-chain restricted by flow) with NO epithelial differentiation (cytokeratin AE1/AE3 negative, GATA3 negative), no cohesive nests, no glands, no single-file infiltration; there is no breast mass on exam or on the 2026-03 mammogram and no FDG-avid breast lesion on PET-CT; and the disease pattern (FDG-avid left axillary, mediastinal, mesenteric conglomerate, para-aortic nodes, multiple FDG-avid splenic nodules; SUVmax 22.3 in the mesenteric mass) is that of lymphoma, not breast carcinoma. Her breast cancer remains in remission (mammogram 2026-03-02 BI-RADS 2).

Subtype and biology: DLBCL, NOS, non-germinal-center B-cell (activated B-cell-like) type by the Hans algorithm (CD10 negative, BCL6 positive, MUM1/IRF4 positive in ~80% of cells). CD5 negative, cyclin D1 negative, CD30 negative, EBER-ISH negative, Ki-67 ~80%, focal necrosis, elevated LDH 510 U/L. Double-expressor by immunohistochemistry (MYC 45%, BCL2 70%) BUT NOT double-hit: interphase FISH on 2026-09-08 shows no MYC (8q24), BCL2 (18q21) or BCL6 (3q27) rearrangement. Therefore this is not 'DLBCL/high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements' and the first-line approach is unchanged. The 2022 ICC/WHO 'DLBCL, NOS' category applies (not EBV-associated, not BCL2-rearranged, not IRF4-rearranged, no blastoid/gray-zone morphology).

Prior therapy: dose-dense doxorubicin 60 mg/m2 + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2 x4 (cumulative doxorubicin 240 mg/m2) then weekly paclitaxel x12, with 50 Gy + 10 Gy boost to the left breast in 2016 - a recognized risk factor for therapy-related lymphoma/AML 5-10 years later. Her morphology and immunophenotype do NOT support therapy-related classification (EBV negative, no antecedent lymphoproliferative disorder, normocellular marrow with trilineage hematopoiesis and no dysplasia, no cytopenias other than mild anemia), so I am classifying this as DLBCL, NOS rather than therapy-related DLBCL. She has no known germline risk indication: FISH is negative, so NCCN-directed germline BCL2/BCL6 testing is not indicated, and her family history (father with colon cancer at 74, mother with heart failure) does not meet criteria for hereditary breast/ovarian testing.
answer.stage:
Ann Arbor/Lugano stage III with splenic involvement and B symptoms (IIISB) - disseminated disease - with the caveat below.

Disease map (PET-CT 2026-09-08): left axillary nodes 2.2 cm, SUVmax 17.8 (adjacent to post-excision change); mediastinal prevascular and left paratracheal nodes 2.9 cm, SUVmax 15.4; mesenteric nodal conglomerate 7.5 x 5.1 cm, SUVmax 22.3; para-aortic nodes 3.0 cm, SUVmax 16.9; spleen 12.8 cm with multiple FDG-avid nodules, largest 2.1 cm, SUVmax 16.2. Nodal disease both above and below the diaphragm plus splenic parenchymal involvement; no FDG-avid disease in liver, adrenals, kidneys, lungs, bone, marrow or breasts; no pleural or pericardial effusion; no ascites; no FDG-avid pelvic or inguinal nodes.

Bone marrow (core + aspirate flow, 2026-09-08): NEGATIVE - normocellular for age (~40%) with trilineage hematopoiesis, no lymphoma on morphology or CD20/PAX5 immunostains, no monotypic B-cell population on flow. So there is no marrow involvement; the splenic lesions are the only extranodal disease.

Staging caveat that I want the board to note: under Lugano the spleen is a lymphoid organ, so the strict stage is III-S (stage III nodes both sides of diaphragm + spleen). If the splenic parenchymal nodules are counted as extranodal organ involvement (a common practice variation and how the outside CT impression was framed), the stage is IV-S. This distinction is purely academic here: both are stage >= III, so NCCN-IPI (stage III/IV = 1 point), CNS-IPI (stage III/IV = 1 point) and the treatment plan are identical. I will document it as stage III-S (B) / IV-S, B symptoms.

B symptoms: present - recurrent evening fevers to 38.4 C (self-documented, no infectious source), drenching night sweats 2-3 nights weekly requiring change of nightclothes, fatigue, and 3.7% unintentional weight loss (72.8 kg March 2026 -> 70.5 kg 2026-09-01 -> 70.1 kg 2026-09-17; note this is below the >10% weight-loss threshold, so the B designation rests on fever and night sweats).

Bulky disease: the largest nodal mass is 7.5 cm, so it is NOT bulky by the NCCN >= 10 cm criterion, although the mesenteric conglomerate is large by other conventions and is the main driver of tumor lysis risk. No testicular, skin, bone, CNS, or breast involvement identified. No documented testicular examination exists (PET is insensitive there) - to be done at the next visit.
answer.biology:
Summary of the immunophenotype and what it means for management:

- Lineage: mature B-cell. CD20 diffuse/strong positive, PAX5 positive, CD19 positive, kappa light-chain restricted (62% of events) by flow cytometry; CD3 negative in tumor cells, CD5 negative. Diagnosis: DLBCL, NOS.
- Subtype: non-germinal-center B-cell-like (activated B-cell-like) by Hans (CD10 negative, BCL6 positive, MUM1/IRF4 positive ~80%). This does not currently change standard therapy, but it is an adverse biologic feature and it raises (not lowers) the probability of relapse.
- Proliferation and grade: Ki-67 ~80%, numerous mitoses, focal necrosis - high-grade.
- Double-expressor vs double-hit: MYC positive in ~45% of cells (>=40%) and BCL2 positive in ~70% (>=50%) satisfies the IHC double-expressor definition, but break-apart FISH (200 nuclei, 2026-09-08) shows NO MYC, BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangement. This distinction is the single most important biology point in this case: IHC double-expressor status does NOT constitute double-hit lymphoma, does not require high-dose methotrexate or intensified chemotherapy, does not mandate CNS prophylaxis, and does not change first-line management. NCCN-directed FISH has been done as required for IHC double-expressors, and because FISH is negative, NCCN does not recommend germline BCL2/BCL6 counseling/testing here.
- EBER negative; CD30 negative; cyclin D1 negative; no evidence of EBV-driven or double-hit biology.
- Supportive biology: elevated LDH 510 U/L (normal 182 in March 2026; roughly 2.5-2.8x ULN), beta-2 microglobulin 2.9 mg/L (mildly high), normocellular marrow with trilineage hematopoiesis and adequate iron stores, Hgb 11.4 g/dL (mild anemia of chronic disease), normal WBC/ANC/platelets, normal renal and hepatic function (creatinine 0.8, eGFR 85, albumin 3.8, AST 24, ALT 22, ALP 92, bilirubin 0.6), uric acid 5.8, calcium 9.3. HIV, HBsAg, anti-HBc, anti-HBs and HCV antibody all non-reactive. Normal cardiac MRI/echocardiogram is NOT normal: LVEF 45% (down from 62% in 2016), GLS -14%, grade I diastolic dysfunction, mild MR - this is treated as a cardiotoxicity risk modifier, not as biology.
- Not demonstrated, and why it does not change my plan: no FISH-confirmed rearrangements, no morphologic features of transformation from occult follicular lymphoma (no follicular pattern, CD10 negative, marrow clean, no BCL2/BCL6 rearrangement), no features of EBV-associated or chronic-inflammation-associated DLBCL.
- Uncertainties: the MYC IHC of 45% is borderline and I want expert hematopathology review to confirm the double-expressor call and to exclude a gray-zone or blastoid phenotype; I also want to make sure the 2016 sentinel nodes and blocks are reviewed for any antecedent follicular clone, since transformation would change the approach (and would raise the question of FISH on the marrow). Neither of these is expected to change the regimen if confirmed negative.
answer.prognosis:
Risk scores (computed from the record): NCCN-IPI 4 (high-intermediate risk) = elevated LDH with ratio >= 1.5x ULN (1) + ECOG >= 1 (1) + stage III/IV (1) + age > 60 (0, she is 59) + extranodal sites > 1 (0, the spleen is her only extranodal site and the marrow is negative). Standardized 5-year overall survival for NCCN-IPI 4-5 is approximately 50-55%. IPI is 2 (low-intermediate) and age-adjusted IPI is 2, because she is < 60 with ECOG 1 - the IPI understates risk here, which is exactly why I am using NCCN-IPI and will communicate a 50-60% probability of cure with R-CHOP rather than the more reassuring IPI 2 number.

Favorable: no double-hit biology, marrow uninvolved, no bulky >= 10 cm disease, no CNS or testicular involvement, ECOG 1, young age (59), preserved marrow and organ function, negative PET elsewhere, and - importantly for a relapse - she is a strong candidate for autologous transplant and for CD19-directed CAR-T if she is refractory.

Adverse: stage IV-equivalent (disseminated nodal disease plus splenic involvement), B symptoms, elevated LDH ~2.5-2.8x ULN, non-GCB (activated B-cell-like) subtype, IHC double-expressor phenotype (MYC 45% / BCL2 70%), high Ki-67 80%, and a 7.5 cm mesenteric conglomerate with high SUVmax (22.3) implying a high proliferation rate and substantial cytoreduction requirement.

Competing (non-lymphoma) mortality risk - which in this patient may be the most modifiable prognostic factor: baseline LVEF 45% with GLS -14% after cumulative doxorubicin 240 mg/m2 and left breast/chest irradiation, in a patient with a mother who had heart failure. Anthracycline-induced cardiomyopathy with future heart failure is a real competing risk to both cure and long-term survival; protecting her heart is therefore part of treating her lymphoma successfully, not an afterthought. Her other medical problems (HTN 148/90 on amlodipine, osteopenia T-score -1.8, penicillin allergy with hives) are minor and manageable.

Expected natural history with R-CHOP: roughly 55-65% probability of cure, with relapse concentrated in the first 2 years (~30-35% risk); early relapse or primary refractoriness is the dominant failure mode, and both are salvageable (R-DHAP, R-ICE without bleomycin, or R-GDP followed by autologous stem cell transplant if chemosensitive; or CD19 CAR-T axi-cel/liso-cel, which in relapsed/refractory DLBCL confers roughly 40-50% long-term survival in eligible patients and, in her case, would also spare her further anthracycline). I will discuss these numbers plainly with her and her husband, framed as 'most likely cured, with a well-defined backup plan if not'.
answer.first_line_treatment:
DECISION: full-dose R-CHOP-21 for 6 cycles, every 21 days, with pegfilgrastim support, an interim PET-CT after cycle 3, and an end-of-treatment PET-CT 6-8 weeks after cycle 6. Regimen: rituximab 375 mg/m2 IV day 1, cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2 IV day 1, doxorubicin 50 mg/m2 IV day 1, vincristine 1.4 mg/m2 (capped at 2 mg) IV day 1, prednisone 100 mg days 1-5. BSA 1.79 m2. Cycle 1 to start as soon as cycle 1 is safe (she has no infection and her marrow is clean; I do not intend to wait beyond the tumor board for any further result).

Why R-CHOP and 6 cycles: this is the only regimen with proven curative intent in DLBCL NOS in a fit patient, and she is fit (ECOG 1, working, independent, normal marrow/renal/hepatic function). I am NOT using dose-dense R-CHOP-14, dose-adjusted EPOCH-R, upfront CAR-T or upfront autologous transplant, none of which add benefit in first-line DLBCL without double-hit biology. I am not planning 8 cycles up front because the largest mass is 7.5 cm (not bulky by the >= 10 cm NCCN definition); I will extend to 8 cycles only if the interim PET is not a complete metabolic response or if significant residual disease persists at the end of treatment. No maintenance therapy is planned (no benefit in DLBCL). No consolidative radiotherapy is planned now; I would consider it only for a single localized residual site after chemotherapy.

THE CARDIAC QUESTION, WHICH IS THE REAL DECISION AT THIS BOARD: her prior cumulative doxorubicin (240 mg/m2) plus left breast irradiation, with LVEF 45% (from 62%) and GLS -14%, is the strongest reason to pause. My decision is to proceed with FULL-DOSE R-CHOP including doxorubicin, under a hard cardiac safety net, rather than to substitute an anthracycline-free regimen. Reasons: she has no heart failure symptoms (no orthopnea, no edema, normal JVP, NYHA I, RSVP 28, no effusion), her decline is mild and asymptomatic, and the efficacy loss of omitting anthracycline is large (R-CVP and R-mini-CHOP have materially worse cure rates). The safety net: (1) cardiology co-management before cycle 1, including a CAD work-up she has never had (she has no prior stress test or coronary imaging), NT-proBNP, and MUGA or repeat echo with GLS for a reproducible baseline, with cardiac MRI if the mechanism of the EF decline is unclear; (2) start lisinopril (or ramipril) plus carvedilol or metoprolol succinate now, and tighten BP to < 130/80 (her BP is 148/90 on amlodipine 5 mg - I will increase amlodipine to 10 mg); (3) dexrazoxane 250-500 mg/m2 with each doxorubicin dose to reduce anthracycline cardiotoxicity (no increased second-malignancy signal in DLBCL data); (4) echocardiogram with GLS after cycles 2, 4 and 6, with pre-specified rules - hold and reassess doxorubicin if LVEF falls below 40% or more than 10 points from baseline, if new/worsening heart failure symptoms appear, or if a new regional wall-motion abnormality appears; if anthracycline is judged unsafe I will switch to R-CVP (or R-CHOP with doxorubicin omitted), not stop curative therapy; (5) daily weights and strict fluid balance with symptom-triggered diuresis; no other anthracycline/anthraquinone, no trastuzumab, no VEGF inhibitor.

Interim PET-adapted plan (cycle 3, week 10-12): Deauville 1-3 -> complete 6 cycles. Deauville 4-5 -> biopsy the PET-avid site to separate residual lymphoma from inflammation before changing therapy; biopsy negative -> finish 6 cycles (add 2 if residual disease); biopsy positive -> treat as primary refractory: salvage (R-DHAP, R-ICE, or R-GDP) with autologous transplant if chemosensitive, or CD19 CAR-T (axi-cel or liso-cel) - in her case I would favor CAR-T if she is refractory, because it avoids further anthracycline and she is young and fit. End-of-treatment PET 4-5 -> biopsy any PET-avid residual site before escalating, and consider consolidative RT for a single localized residual site.

Refractory/relapsed contingency: she is a good candidate for autologous transplant and for CD19 CAR-T (ECOG 1, marrow uninvolved, organ function preserved). I would avoid bleomycin-containing salvage (R-CHOP-14, R-EPOCH-R, ICE with bleomycin) because of the mild left anterior lung fibrosis in the prior radiation field on PET and the cumulative cardiopulmonary risk; R-DHAP, R-GDP, or CAR-T are preferred.

Her breast cancer is not a competing treatment driver: the AI is not being changed for lymphoma reasons (see supportive_care), no further breast surgery or radiotherapy is planned, and her breast surveillance continues with breast oncology.
answer.cns_risk:
DECISION: no routine intrathecal CNS prophylaxis and no baseline brain MRI at this time; I will obtain an MRI brain with and without contrast immediately for ANY neurologic symptom, and I will perform and document a testicular examination at the next visit (PET is insensitive to testicular lymphoma).

Risk stratification: CNS-IPI = 3 (intermediate risk). Components: age > 60 = 0 (she is 59); LDH elevated = 1; ECOG >= 1 = 1; stage >= III = 1; extranodal sites > 1 = 0 (the spleen is the only extranodal site and marrow is negative); kidney or adrenal involvement = 0 (both normal on CT and PET). NCCN criteria for CNS prophylaxis in DLBCL are: testicular involvement; MYC/BCL2-rearranged (double-hit) disease; high-risk extranodal sites (breast, adrenal, kidney/GI tract, bone marrow); CNS-IPI high risk (4-6); or CNS-IPI 3 (intermediate) with additional high-risk features. She meets NONE of these: FISH is negative for MYC, BCL2 and BCL6; her only extranodal site is the spleen (not one of the high-risk sites); kidneys and adrenals are clear; there is no lymphoma involvement of the breast (her prior breast cancer is separate, in remission, with no FDG-avid breast lesion on PET); and she is neurologically asymptomatic with a non-focal examination.

Where I am uncertain, and the honest middle ground: she does have stage IV-equivalent disease, elevated LDH, and a second malignancy, and PET cannot evaluate the brain, so a small sanctuary-site risk remains that staging cannot exclude. If the board prefers maximum caution, the acceptable addition is intrathecal cytarabine during cycles 3-5 (I would use cytarabine rather than methotrexate, to avoid additive neurotoxicity with concurrent vincristine) plus a baseline MRI brain. I would not add IT methotrexate in a patient receiving vincristine, and I would not add prophylaxis on the basis of the IHC double-expressor phenotype alone, since the FISH is negative and CNS-IPI is only intermediate.

Decision triggers that would change this plan: a neurologic symptom at any point (MRI brain, and if lymphoma is confirmed, treat with HD-MTX-based CNS-directed therapy and switch to a CNS-penetrating systemic regimen); demonstration of testicular involvement (then IT prophylaxis becomes mandatory and I would add a testicular ultrasound/FDG-PET and consider CNS-penetrating agents); new FDG-avid disease in the breast, adrenal glands, kidney, GI tract or marrow (any of these raises the CNS-IPI to 4-5 and makes IT prophylaxis appropriate); or a positive interim PET, which would prompt CNS re-evaluation. Note also that her prior breast radiation field does not include the brain, so there is no iatrogenic CNS risk factor.
answer.response_assessment:
DECISION: interim PET-CT after cycle 3 (week 10-12 of R-CHOP), end-of-treatment PET-CT 6-8 weeks after cycle 6 (after resolution of treatment-related inflammation), then surveillance by history/physical and CBC, with PET only if clinically indicated. Lugano response criteria with Deauville scoring throughout.

Baseline for comparison (2026-09-08): mesenteric conglomerate 7.5 x 5.1 cm, SUVmax 22.3; splenic nodules largest 2.1 cm, SUVmax 16.2; left axillary 2.2 cm, SUVmax 17.8; para-aortic 3.0 cm, SUVmax 16.9; mediastinal 2.9 cm, SUVmax 15.4.

Interim (after cycle 3): Deauville 1-3 = complete metabolic response (CMR) -> complete the planned 6 cycles. Deauville 4-5 with >= 50% reduction in the sum of products of diameters of PET-positive lesions and no new disease = partial metabolic response -> I will biopsy the site with the highest SUV (or a PET-avid site) to distinguish active lymphoma from radiation change, inflammation or splenosis; I will not escalate therapy on imaging alone. Deauville 4-5 with a new lesion or rising SUV = progression -> refractory pathway (biopsy, then salvage with or without CAR-T). Deauville 1-3 with a growing non-avid mass is unusual; I would re-image in 6 weeks rather than act.

End of treatment: PET-CT 6-8 weeks after the last dose. Deauville 1-3 = complete response regardless of residual CT size (this matters for her residual 2 cm left axillary node and the mesenteric conglomerate). Deauville 4-5 with >= 50% decrease = partial response -> biopsy any PET-avid residual before further therapy, and consider consolidative radiotherapy if a single localized site persists. I will not biopsy PET-negative residual masses. No repeat bone marrow biopsy is needed if the end-of-treatment PET is negative (her marrow was negative at baseline and PET is insensitive for marrow, so a negative PET plus the negative baseline marrow suffices).

Surveillance after CR: history, examination, CBC and LDH every 2-3 months for 1 year, then every 6 months; optional PET-CT at ~12 weeks post-treatment and thereafter only if clinically indicated; annual mammogram with breast oncology (her mammographic sensitivity is reduced by prior chest irradiation and by anastrozole - mammogram planned in the fall of 2026 and yearly thereafter); DEXA in 2027; continued echo with GLS surveillance as above. If she relapses: repeat PET-CT, biopsy, and bone marrow before salvage, and re-assess for CAR-T eligibility - she will already have been consented to that pathway.

What would change the plan: a positive interim PET with a positive biopsy (refractory pathway), Deauville 4-5 at end of treatment (biopsy and consider RT or salvage), or an EF decline forcing anthracycline omission, which would change both the regimen and the response interpretation and make closer (cycle-level) assessment more important.
answer.pretreatment_workup:
COMPLETED (reviewed and adequate): excisional biopsy of the left axillary node 2026-08-25 with morphology, full IHC panel, flow cytometry and interphase FISH (MYC/BCL2/BCL6, 2026-09-08); PET-CT 2026-09-08; bone marrow core biopsy and aspirate flow 2026-09-08; CBC with differential 2026-09-01 (Hgb 11.4, WBC 6.9, ANC 4.6, ALC 1.2, platelets 178); CMP 2026-09-01 (creatinine 0.8, eGFR 85, Ca 9.3, albumin 3.8, AST 24, ALT 22, ALP 92, bili 0.6, glucose 96); LDH 510; beta-2 microglobulin 2.9; uric acid 5.8; phosphate 3.6; HIV Ag/Ab, HBsAg, anti-HBc, anti-HBs, HCV Ab all non-reactive; transthoracic echocardiogram 2026-09-08 (LVEF 45%, GLS -14%, grade I diastolic dysfunction, mild MR, RVSP 28); ECOG 1; mammogram 2026-03-02 BI-RADS 2 and no FDG-avid breast lesion on PET; full general, breast, abdominal and neurologic examination documented; no testicular examination documented (PET is insensitive to testicular lymphoma) and no brain imaging.

TO BE COMPLETED BEFORE CYCLE 1: (1) baseline ECG (none on file) with electrolytes - required before anthracycline and for monitoring; (2) cardiology consultation with structured pre-anthracycline risk assessment: CAD evaluation (she has never had one despite hypertension and a family history of heart failure), NT-proBNP, and MUGA or repeat echo with GLS for the most reproducible baseline, with cardiac MRI if the mechanism of the LVEF decline remains unclear - this determines whether full-dose doxorubicin is safe and how the regimen will be modified; (3) start lisinopril or ramipril plus carvedilol or metoprolol succinate, and optimize BP to < 130/80 (increase amlodipine to 10 mg); (4) serum quantitative immunoglobulins (IgG, IgA, IgM) before rituximab, with a plan to monitor and replace (IVIG) if IgG falls below 400 mg/dL or she has recurrent infections; (5) vaccination - hepatitis B vaccination series now (anti-HBs is negative, so she is non-immune and this is the one actionable gap with a clear timeline; ideally >= 4 weeks before immunosuppression), 2026-27 influenza, updated COVID-19, pneumococcal (PCV20/PCV21), and recombinant zoster (Shingrix, non-live); NO live vaccines during therapy (no BCG, no oral polio, no live zoster); (6) iron studies, reticulocyte count, vitamin B12 and folate to characterize the Hgb of 11.4 g/dL (presumed anemia of chronic disease with clean marrow), plus a repeat CBC, LDH and CMP immediately before cycle 1; (7) confirm menopausal status and, if she is not clearly postmenopausal, a pregnancy test; document fertility counselling (likely not actionable at 59 but should be recorded); (8) tumor lysis risk setup - baseline uric acid, creatinine, K, Ca, phosphate, LDH and urine output are available; begin allopurinol 300 mg daily 2-3 days before cycle 1 with hydration, and check G6PD only if rasburicase is needed; (9) document baseline peripheral neuropathy examination, bowel regimen (senna/docusate plus osmotic laxative) and ocular history before vincristine; (10) dental/oral assessment before corticosteroid-containing therapy; (11) nutritional assessment and intervention for the 3.7% weight loss and the bulky mesenteric disease (dietitian, high-calorie/high-protein, symptom-directed GI review, and monitoring for bowel symptoms as the mesenteric mass involutes); (12) document a full neurologic examination and a testicular examination; (13) baseline DEXA (last 2025, T-score -1.8) and an explicit bone-protection plan given osteopenia plus ongoing anastrozole plus prednisone; (14) written shared decision with the patient and her husband covering treatment intensity, the cardiac stop rules, and the refractory-disease pathway (salvage vs CAR-T vs palliation).

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, WITH REASONS: no repeat bone marrow biopsy (PET and marrow are both negative for marrow disease); no marrow cytogenetics (normocellular marrow, no dysplasia, no cytopenias - I will add cytogenetics if counts later fall atypically, given her prior alkylator/anthracycline exposure); no germline BCL2/BCL6 testing (FISH negative - NCCN recommends this only when BCL2/BCL6 rearrangement is identified); no prophylactic CNS prophylaxis (see cns_risk); no PET-CT of the brain (I am not pursuing CNS prophylaxis in an asymptomatic patient with intermediate CNS-IPI, and MRI will be obtained for any neurologic symptom); no breast MRI (mammogram benign and PET negative in both breasts); no surgical intervention for the residual 2 cm left axillary node (FDG-avid and expected to respond to systemic therapy).

COORDINATION: breast oncology has been informed that the DLBCL is a new primary and that her breast cancer remains in remission; breast surveillance continues on its own schedule; the AI decision below is coordinated with breast oncology; the left axillary surgical site needs no further intervention. Patient identity/documentation for her work and insurance authorization for 6 cycles of R-CHOP plus growth factor support should be arranged now so cycle 1 is not delayed.
answer.supportive_care:
CARDIAC (the priority): cardiology co-management; lisinopril or ramipril plus carvedilol or metoprolol succinate started now; BP target < 130/80 (increase amlodipine 5 mg to 10 mg as needed); echocardiogram with GLS after cycles 2, 4 and 6; daily weights and strict I/O during admissions; dexrazoxane 250-500 mg/m2 with each doxorubicin dose; no other anthracycline, no trastuzumab, no VEGF inhibitor; symptom-triggered diuresis; no routine IVIG (see immunology below).

HEMATOLOGIC: pegfilgrastim 6 mg SC 24-72 hours after each cycle (primary prophylaxis is indicated given stage III/IV disease, high tumor burden and prior cytotoxic therapy); CBC weekly during nadir; transfusion support as needed. The Hgb of 11.4 should be characterized (iron studies, retic, B12/folate) and should improve as the lymphoma responds.

TUMOR LYSIS SYNDROME: allopurinol 300 mg daily (adjust to renal function) starting 2-3 days before cycle 1 and continued through the first 2 cycles; oral/IV hydration 2.5-3 L/day; monitor K, Ca, phosphate, creatinine, uric acid, LDH and urine output for 24 hours after each cycle during the highest-risk window (the 7.5 cm mesenteric conglomerate with SUVmax 22.3 is the main risk driver); rasburicase only if urate rises or hyperphosphatemia develops (check G6PD first); watch the mesenteric mass closely for bowel pain, bleeding or obstruction as a marker of rapid response and of the rare risk of infarction/lysis of the conglomerate.

ANTIEMETIC AND INFUSION SUPPORT: aprepitant + ondansetron + dexamethasone with each cycle (avoid stacking extra dexamethasone on top of R-CHOP prednisone where possible); rituximab premedication with acetaminophen 650 mg, cetirizine (not diphenhydramine - she works and should stay alert) and corticosteroid; first dose in a monitored setting with slow infusion and epinephrine available; a written plan for managing infusion reactions.

INFECTION PREVENTION: TMP-SMX one double-strength tablet daily for Pneumocystis prophylaxis (after confirming counts and potassium/creatinine); acyclovir 400 mg twice daily if mucositis or prolonged neutropenia; for antifungal prophylaxis use fluconazole 200 mg daily or an echinocandin - I will AVOID itraconazole, voriconazole and posaconazole with R-CHOP because CYP3A4 inhibition raises vincristine exposure and neurotoxicity risk (and because of interaction potential with anastrozole); neutropenic precautions, hand hygiene, and prompt same-day review for any temperature >= 38.0 C; her current fevers should be interpreted as B symptoms and expected to resolve with treatment, but infection must be excluded (repeat CBC, blood cultures, examination) before starting myelosuppressive therapy; institutional neutropenic diet advice and avoidance of raw/undercooked food; she has splenic involvement, so fever requires urgent review, and pneumococcal vaccination is important - routine prophylactic antibiotics are not indicated unless she becomes functionally asplenic; vincristine constipation prophylaxis (senna/docusate plus an osmotic laxative), monitoring for peripheral neuropathy and for hyponatremia, with dose reduction or omission of vincristine if neuropathy becomes functionally limiting.

ENDOCRINE AND BONE - HER QUESTION ABOUT ANASTROZOLE: DECISION - continue anastrozole 1 mg daily through R-CHOP and complete the planned 10-year course in November 2026, then stop permanently. Reasoning: she has only ~3 months of the course left and the benefit of adjuvant endocrine therapy is front-loaded in the first 5 years, so interrupting now has minimal oncologic consequence either way; anastrozole has no clinically meaningful interaction with R-CHOP and no cardiotoxicity; her osteopenia makes continued bone-directed care (calcium/vitamin D, weight-bearing and resistance exercise, DEXA) the relevant issue rather than the AI itself; and stopping it would predictably add arthralgias and fatigue without benefit. If her fatigue or arthralgias become limiting I will hold it (a hold of even several months carries minimal oncologic risk) - that is a shared decision with her, and breast oncology should be copied. I will not restart anastrozole after November 2026 unless breast oncology identifies a new indication. Bone health: continue calcium 600 mg/vitamin D3 800 IU twice daily; restart adapted weight-bearing and resistance exercise (she has stopped her exercise classes and both bone and function matter); DEXA 2027; consider zoledronic acid only if the T-score worsens while on the AI; prednisone 100 mg x 5 days x 6 cycles is a modest total exposure but justifies the above.

OTHER: no live vaccines during therapy (recombinant and inactivated vaccines are safe and should be given at the appropriate times); PPI as needed for GI protection; limit acetaminophen to <= 2 g/day and avoid NSAIDs (cytopenia, renal, and hepatic considerations with R-CHOP); limit alcohol; psycho-oncology referral (a second malignancy plus her mother's heart failure anxiety) and supportive/palliative care co-management for symptom control alongside curative treatment; social work for work and family logistics (her husband drives her to all visits); occupational therapy input on neuropathy and stamina for library work; no routine antifungal or antiviral beyond the above; mammography per breast oncology; age-appropriate colorectal cancer screening (average risk - her father with colon cancer at 74 does not create a hereditary indication).
answer.fitness_and_goals:
FITNESS: fit for curative-intent combination chemotherapy. ECOG 1; NYHA class I (climbs two flights of stairs without stopping); independent in all activities; still working full-time as a school librarian; BMI 25.7 (70.1 kg, 165 cm); BSA 1.79 m2; no uncontrolled medical condition, no active infection, no neurologic symptoms; marrow preserved (platelets 178, ANC 4.6, no cytopenias other than Hgb 11.4); renal and hepatic function normal (creatinine 0.8, eGFR 85, albumin 3.8); no diabetes, no prior coronary disease, no arrhythmia; no venous thromboembolism history. Her limited reserves are cardiopulmonary: LVEF 45% with GLS -14% and grade I diastolic dysfunction after 240 mg/m2 doxorubicin and left breast irradiation, plus mild left anterior lung fibrosis in the prior radiation field on PET (relevant later because it excludes bleomycin-containing salvage regimens) - but no heart failure symptoms, no edema, normal JVP, RVSP 28, no effusions. There is no frailty, no malnutrition and no reason to dose-reduce or to use R-mini-CHOP.

GOALS (as documented on 2026-09-17): she wants treatment aimed at cure and hopes to return to full-time work at the school library. She is the primary decision-maker, her husband accompanies her and drives her to all visits, and she has two adult children. She asked directly whether the echocardiogram changes her treatment and whether she should keep taking anastrozole; she is anxious about her heart because her mother had heart failure. Fear of recurrence from a second primary and a second round of chemotherapy is the dominant emotional issue and should be named explicitly at the board.

PLAN AGAINST THOSE GOALS: R-CHOP x6 over about 4.5 months is the regimen most likely to achieve durable cure and return her to work; the cardiac safeguards above are the price of that decision and are acceptable to her. The most likely treatment-limiting toxicity for her job is vincristine neuropathy, so I will document a baseline neurologic examination, use a laxative regimen, monitor closely and reduce or omit vincristine if neuropathy limits her ability to work, and involve occupational therapy. B symptoms, fatigue and the 7.5 cm mesenteric mass should improve with treatment, which should support her functional recovery. On the heart: I will tell her plainly that the fall in LVEF from 62% to 45% is most likely anthracycline- and radiation-related cardiomyopathy, that it does NOT preclude R-CHOP, that it does raise her long-term risk of heart failure, that this is exactly why cardiology, an ACE inhibitor, a beta blocker and serial echocardiograms are part of the plan, and that she should obtain her family's cardiac history so that her children's screening can be considered. She should also understand that her mother's heart failure raises, rather than lowers, the value of protecting her heart now. I will document the shared decision to proceed with full-dose R-CHOP with the heart team involved, and I will revisit it after cycle 2, when the first on-treatment echocardiogram and the interim PET are both available. If the EF falls or symptoms develop, my commitment is to modify the regimen (omit doxorubicin) rather than to abandon curative therapy. If the disease proves refractory, her stated goals support an aggressive salvage/CAR-T pathway rather than early palliation, and I will have that conversation in advance so it is not a crisis decision.
missing_information: No baseline ECG is on file - required before anthracycline and for ongoing QT/electrolyte monitoring; this should be obtained before cycle 1.

No cardiology consultation or structured pre-anthracycline cardiac risk assessment is documented. The mechanism of the LVEF decline (anthracycline + left breast RT vs. occult obstructive coronary disease) has not been established: no stress test, coronary CT/angiography, NT-proBNP or troponin, and no MUGA or cardiac MRI. The board must decide on the modality for serial EF/GLS monitoring, on dexrazoxane, and on whether full-dose doxorubicin is acceptable.

No serum quantitative immunoglobulins (IgG/IgA/IgM) before rituximab, and no plan documented for monitoring or replacing hypogammaglobulinemia - relevant given her 10 years of endocrine therapy and her planned B-cell-depleting therapy.

Menopausal status, pregnancy test, contraceptive counselling and fertility assessment are not documented; the record does not state whether she is still menstruating at 59, which bears on both the anastrozole discussion and chemotherapy counselling.

No documented testicular examination and no baseline brain MRI - both are sites where PET is insensitive. My plan is a testicular exam at the next visit and symptom-triggered MRI, but these baseline examinations should be recorded, and I should be asked to confirm the board accepts that approach.

The laboratory report does not state the LDH upper limit of normal, so the exact LDH ratio (and hence the NCCN-IPI score of 4) cannot be independently verified; no formal IPI, NCCN-IPI or CNS-IPI calculation is recorded anywhere in the chart.

Iron studies, reticulocyte count, vitamin B12 and folate were not reported for the hemoglobin of 11.4 g/dL - the anemia has not been characterized (anemia of chronic disease is presumed; the marrow is negative), and no repeat CBC or LDH has been drawn since 2026-09-01, so she enters treatment without a current count.

Hepatitis B vaccination has not been started and she is non-immune (anti-HBs negative) - an actionable gap with a timing requirement of roughly 4 weeks before immunosuppression; influenza 2026-27, updated COVID-19, pneumococcal and recombinant zoster vaccination status and timing are also not documented.

No documented baseline neurologic examination, neuropathy grading, bowel regimen plan or ocular history before vincristine - needed both for toxicity monitoring and for interpreting any future neurologic symptom; no dental or oral assessment before corticosteroid-containing therapy.

No nutrition assessment or dietary intervention plan for the 3.7% unintentional weight loss and the bulky mesenteric disease (dietitian review, symptom-directed GI assessment, monitoring for bowel complications as the mass involutes) - and no documentation that infection has been excluded as a cause of her fevers (no repeat CBC, no blood cultures) before myelosuppressive therapy is started.

No expert hematopathology second review is documented for the borderline MYC immunohistochemistry (45%) and the double-expressor designation, nor for completeness of the work-up to exclude occult follicular transformation (no CD21/CD23 or additional follicular markers reported, and no comparison with the 2016 sentinel nodes or blocks).

No DEXA within the last 12 months (last 2025, lumbar T-score -1.8) and no written bone-protection plan before prednisone plus the final months of an aromatase inhibitor; no formal fracture-risk assessment.

No documented shared-decision or advance-care discussion about the refractory/relapsed pathway (salvage chemotherapy versus CD19 CAR-T versus palliation) and what she would want if the disease proves refractory; no palliative-care co-management plan, and no documentation of her understanding of prognosis and of the ~50-60% probability of cure.

No baseline G6PD level (conditionally required if rasburicase becomes necessary) and no documented plan for the sequencing of allopurinol, hydration and uric acid monitoring around the bulky mesenteric mass.

No documented confirmation that the tumor board date (2026-09-18) does not delay cycle 1 unnecessarily, and no documentation of the patient's informed consent to full-dose R-CHOP with its cardiac implications, the pre-specified cardiac stop rules, and the blood-pressure target of < 130/80.

items.criterion: The response states the diagnosis is diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (NOS) with a non-germinal-center (non-GCB) phenotype by the Hans algorithm.
The response notes that Hans non-GCB is an immunohistochemical surrogate and is not equivalent to molecular ABC cell-of-origin by gene-expression profiling.
The response states the left axillary node is lymphoma and not recurrent breast carcinoma (cytokeratin AE1/AE3 and GATA3 negative).
The response stages the disease as Lugano/Ann Arbor stage III (nodes on both sides of the diaphragm with splenic involvement).
The response explains that the spleen is lymphatic tissue (a nodal site), so splenic nodules do not make the disease stage IV, and that there is no non-lymphatic extranodal or marrow involvement.
The response notes B symptoms (documented fevers >38 C and drenching night sweats).
The response notes the 7.5 cm mass is below the 10 cm Lugano bulk threshold, acknowledging that bulk definitions vary (some trials use 7.5 cm).
The response stages this patient as stage IV (e.g. by counting splenic involvement as extranodal disease).
The response classifies the lymphoma as double-expressor by IHC (MYC 45% >=40%, BCL2 70% >=50%) but NOT double-hit (FISH shows no MYC, BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangement).
The response classifies this lymphoma as double-hit / high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements.
The response recommends DA-EPOCH-R (or another intensified regimen) on the basis of double-expressor biology.
The response calculates IPI as 2 (low-intermediate risk): elevated LDH and stage III; age 59, ECOG 1 and no extranodal sites (spleen is not counted as extranodal) score zero.
The response calculates CNS-IPI as 2 (intermediate risk).
The response states that routine CNS prophylaxis is not indicated (CNS-IPI 2, no kidney/adrenal, testicular or breast involvement).
The response mandates CNS prophylaxis (high-dose methotrexate or intrathecal therapy) for this patient.

The response recognizes anthracycline-related cardiac risk (prior doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left chest radiotherapy, LVEF fall from 62% to 45%, i.e. cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction) and does NOT plan standard full-dose doxorubicin (R-CHOP or Pola-R-CHP) without first addressing cardiac function.

The response recommends standard R-CHOP or Pola-R-CHP (full-dose doxorubicin) without conditioning it on the reduced LVEF / prior anthracycline exposure (e.g. without cardio-oncology clearance, a cardioprotective modification, or a non-anthracycline alternative).
The response requests urgent cardio-oncology (or cardiology) evaluation before starting therapy.
The response starts or optimizes guideline-directed cardioprotective therapy: an ACE inhibitor/ARB (or ARNI) plus a beta-blocker (e.g. carvedilol), for example replacing amlodipine.

The response recommends a curative-intent anthracycline-free or anthracycline-modified regimen, e.g. R-CEOP (etoposide in place of doxorubicin) or R-GCVP; R-CHOP with liposomal doxorubicin or dexrazoxane is acceptable only if conditioned on cardio-oncology judging it safe.
The response acknowledges that anthracycline-free regimens likely have lower efficacy than anthracycline-based therapy.
The response plans serial cardiac monitoring during therapy: repeat LVEF/GLS imaging plus troponin and/or natriuretic peptide (BNP/NT-proBNP).
The response recommends palliative-only treatment, best supportive care, or hospice as the plan.
The response plans an end-of-treatment FDG PET-CT read with Lugano criteria / Deauville 5-point scale.
The response assesses tumor lysis risk as low-intermediate (normal creatinine and uric acid, LDH ~2x ULN) and gives allopurinol with hydration for cycle 1.
The response recommends (or reasonably considers) primary G-CSF support with each cycle.
The response addresses the ongoing anastrozole: continuing it is acceptable (no meaningful interaction), or holding it in coordination with breast oncology is also acceptable.
The response confirms hepatitis B serology was checked (HBsAg and anti-HBc nonreactive) before rituximab.
The response judges the patient fit for curative-intent therapy (ECOG 1, normal organ function apart from the LVEF) and acknowledges her goal of cure.
The response lists the cause of the LVEF decline / cardio-oncology work-up as missing (e.g. ischemic evaluation given prior left chest radiotherapy, cardiac MRI, baseline troponin and NT-proBNP).
